# PREFIX-703-R6 — Strictly convex BRC optimal-value envelope and finite algebraic moment-transition parameters

Date: 2026-11-11 (Asia/Shanghai).
Researcher-ID: `EM-DIRECT-E213F8 / TASK_RESEARCH`.
Research-Activity-ID: `RA-58C713C650E93EC94649BFC0`.
Scientific input (unchanged): `awdawmip/enterprise-math@f42f2906d77f24085c123f3ccfe9667d41caa96d`.
Direct prerequisites: PREFIX-621/622 finite signed first-stop observer, PREFIX-625 strictly increasing coordinate means and optimizer sandwich, PREFIX-700 exact rational corner dominance and strict all-real-q optimizer separation, PREFIX-701 exact universal moment bounds.
Research status: AUTHOR_DERIVED / EXACT_FRACTION_IMPLICATION_CHECKED / UNREVIEWED / NOT_ADMITTED.

## Object and exact polynomial carrier

Let `D=[0,1/2]^2` be the auxiliary probability-parameter square of the two labelled signed-information BRC first-stop streams, not a native two-dimensional spatial plane of X6. The ordered signed path populations and frozen first-stop rules are unchanged. For `x=(p,z) in D` let

```text
mu(x)=E[Y(x)], W(x)=Var(Y(x)),
V_q(x)=q^2 W(x)-q mu(x) (q real >=2),
f_t(x)=W(x)-t mu(x), H(t)=max_{x in D} f_t(x), 0<=t<=1/2.
```

The endpoint `t=0` is the mathematically defined variance-only limit of `t=1/q` as `q->infinity`, rather than another finite operational observation slot. Write `W_*=max_D W`, `A_*=Argmax_D W`, `mu_*=min_{x in A_*}mu(x)` and `L_*={x in A_*:mu(x)=mu_*}`.

Because the first-stop survivor population is finite (0<=n<=188), each survivor `s_n(p)=sum_k a_{n,k}p^k(1-p)^(n-k)` has integer coefficients; the gamma-clock and negative-binomial moment kernels in PREFIX-700 use rational coefficients. Hence `mu,H_2=E[Y^2]/2` are rational bivariate polynomials, with coordinate degree at most 188. Consequently `W=2H_2-mu^2` is rational polynomial with coordinate degree at most 376. This finite exact polynomial property, rather than a fitted approximation, permits quantifier elimination on the compact rational square.

## Theorem 703.1 — Strict convexity over the closed inverse-slot interval

`H:[0,1/2]->R` is continuous, strictly convex and strictly decreasing. In particular, for all `0<=t1<t2<=1/2`, `0<lambda<1`,

```text
H((1-lambda)*t1+lambda*t2)
  < (1-lambda)*H(t1)+lambda*H(t2).
```

Its monotonic decrease is quantitatively bounded by

```text
25*(t2-t1) <= H(t1)-H(t2) <= 378*(t2-t1).
```

**Proof.** Each stream stops after between 25 and 189 informative signs. Its unit Poisson-clock completion time is the sum of that many independent unit-mean exponential waits. Hence `25<=mu(x)<=378`: the maximum of the two completion times is bounded below by either and above by their sum. Compactness ensures all argmax sets are nonempty. For each square corner `c`, PREFIX-700's certified rational intervals give, for `e=(0,1/8)`, `W(e)-W(c)-t(mu(e)-mu(c))>386` for every `0<=t<=1/2`; the companion exact checker verifies the inherited bounds at both endpoints. Thus no corner maximizes any `f_t`, including `t=0`.

Suppose `u` maximizes both `f_s` and `f_t` for `s<t`. At least one coordinate of `u` lies in `(0,1/2)`, since `u` is not a corner. Stationarity in this free coordinate gives `W_i(u)-s mu_i(u)=W_i(u)-t mu_i(u)=0`; subtracting yields `mu_i(u)=0`, contrary to PREFIX-625's strictly positive interior coordinate mean derivative. Thus **different t have disjoint maximizing sets**, also at the limit parameter `t=0`.

For `t_lambda=(1-lambda)s+lambda*t`, choose a maximizer `u` at `t_lambda`. Then
`H(t_lambda)=(1-lambda)f_s(u)+lambda f_t(u)<(1-lambda)H(s)+lambda H(t)`: equality would force the same `u` to maximize at both endpoints, which was excluded. The variation bound follows by inserting an optimizer at either endpoint and `25<=mu<=378`; continuity follows by this Lipschitz bound. QED.

## Theorem 703.2 — Finitely many algebraic parameters can support distinct optimal moment pairs

There is a **finite set `E subset (0,1/2)` consisting of real algebraic numbers** such that, for every `t in (0,1/2)\E`, **all** maximizers of `f_t` share one and the same pair `(mu,W)`. In terms of finite sampling slots, the exceptional set `{q=1/t:t in E}` is also finite and algebraic. Geometric optimizer positions may retain coordinate-permutation symmetry; the uniqueness statement concerns the moment pair.

**Proof.** Define the exact optimizer predicate

```text
Opt(t,x) := x in D AND (forall y in D) f_t(x)>=f_t(y).
E := {t in (0,1/2):
       (exists x,y in D) Opt(t,x) AND Opt(t,y) AND mu(x)!=mu(y)}.
```

The polynomial coefficients and domain endpoints are rational. The first-order formula above has only polynomial inequalities/equalities over Q; real-closed-field quantifier elimination (Tarski–Seidenberg) therefore makes `E` a Q-semialgebraic subset of R.

For any `t in E`, two optimizer points produce two distinct affine supporting functions `f_s(x)` of the convex envelope `H(s)` at `s=t`, with slopes `-mu(x)` different. Consequently `H` is not differentiable at `t`. A convex real function on an interval has at most countably many points of non-differentiability (each left/right-derivative jump admits a distinct rational between its slopes). Thus `E` is countable. A semialgebraic subset of the real line is a finite union of points and intervals; countability forces `E` to be finite. A finite Q-semialgebraic set consists of real algebraic points. For `t not in E`, all optimal means agree by definition, and equality `W-t mu=H(t)` forces all optimal variances to agree as well. QED.

**Finite decision route.** Obtain the frozen rational polynomials from the integer survivor rows, construct the quantified predicate above and run exact real quantifier elimination/CAD to isolate `E`; on each complementary interval the optimal moment pair is single-valued. The theorem establishes finite algebraic reduction; enumerating `E` or deciding whether it is empty is the next computational problem.

## Theorem 703.3 — Lexicographic high-slot limit and explicit variance-loss bound

For **every finite real** `q>=2` and every `x_q in Argmax_D V_q`,

```text
0 < W_*-W(x_q) <= (mu_*-mu(x_q))/q <= 353/q,
mu(x_q) < mu_*.
```

Every accumulation point of any sequence of such maximizers as `q->infinity` belongs to `L_*`. Moreover,

```text
max_D V_q = q^2 W_* - q mu_* + o(q),  q->infinity.
```

**Proof.** Take `u_* in L_*` and `t=1/q>0`. Maximality of `x_q` gives
`W(x_q)-t mu(x_q)>=W_*-t mu_*`, hence
`0<=W_*-W(x_q)<=t(mu_*-mu(x_q))<=353t`.
If `W(x_q)=W_*`, then the inequality forces `mu(x_q)<=mu_*`; by minimality on `A_*`, equality holds and `x_q` maximizes both `f_0` and `f_t`, contradicting Theorem 703.1. So the first inequality is strict and `mu(x_q)<mu_*`.

As `q->infinity`, the explicit inequality forces `W(x_q)->W_*`. Compactness gives accumulation points in `A_*`, with means at most `mu_*`; minimality yields equality, hence every accumulation point lies in `L_*` and `mu(x_q)->mu_*`. Finally
`W_*-t mu_* <= H(t) <= W_*-t mu(x_q)`,
so `H(t)=W_*-t mu_*+o(t)` as `t downarrow0`. Multiply by `q^2` with `t=1/q`. QED.

## Verification, provenance and next unit

`PREFIX703_R6_GLOBAL_VALUE_CHECKS.py` uses Python standard-library `Fraction` to confirm all three inherited corner-bin comparisons uniformly for `0<=t<=1/2`, the 25/378 clock bounds and the coefficient degree accounting, and emits `PREFIX703_R6_RESULTS.json`. Local independent run: `ALL_CHECKS_PASS PREFIX703-R6`. The convexity, semialgebraic finiteness and asymptotic deductions are mathematical proofs in this note, using the pinned ancestor exact-model lemmas and standard real algebraic geometry; the checker does not run CAD or the original 189-row recurrence.

Standard background: Tarski–Seidenberg quantifier elimination and semialgebraic one-variable finite interval/point decomposition (e.g. Basu–Pollack–Roy, *Algorithms in Real Algebraic Geometry*; explanatory sources https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Tarski-Seidenberg+theorem and https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40879-022-00539-3).

**Next discriminating question:** construct `mu,W` rational polynomial coefficients from the frozen 189-row kernel; use exact CAD or rational interval/resultant elimination to determine `E`, especially on `t in [1/24,1/12]`. A certificate that `E` is empty there implies unique optimizer moments for **all** real `q in [12,24]`; the remaining step is localization of actual optimizing positions on the full auxiliary square. Do not infer native spatial or heartbeat dynamics from this observer proof.
